title: Computational Quantification of Mouse Retinal Vasculature Using ImageJ
author: Michel Nader

Sigma is the range or variation in noise. In practice, it is similar to the degree of averaging of the signal by the plugin.

steps.title: Set image scale
steps.instruction: Open the retinal image, choose Analyze → Set Scale…, draw a line over the scale bar with the line tool, enter the known distance and select μm as the unit to define the pixel‑to‑μm conversion.

steps.title: Define measurement parameters
steps.instruction: Select Analyze → Set Measurements…, check Area, Display label, Area fraction and Add to overlay, then confirm.

steps.title: Outline total retinal area
steps.instruction: Select the polygon selection tool, trace the outer border of the retina, add the selection to the overlay (Image → Overlay → Add Selection) and then to the ROI manager (Image → Overlay → To ROI Manager), measure (Analyze → Measure) and record the area value.

steps.title: Outline vascularized retinal area
steps.instruction: Using the polygon tool, trace the vascularized region out to the periphery, add the selection to the overlay and ROI manager as above, ensure the vascular outline is active, then measure (Analyze → Measure) and record the value.

steps.title: Save peripheral and mid‑peripheral ROIs
steps.instruction: For each quadrant of interest, draw a 300 × 800 μm (depth × width) rectangle at the periphery with the Rotated Rectangle tool aligned to the vessel angle, add it to the ROI manager, then draw a second 300 × 800 μm rectangle at the mid‑periphery (midpoint located by drawing a straight line from centre to periphery and noting the overlay label), add it to the ROI manager, repeat for all quadrants, duplicate each ROI to create individual images, and save the images for later processing.

substeps.instruction: Choose a quadrant of interest
Draw peripheral 300 × 800 μm rectangle aligned to vessels
Add peripheral ROI to ROI manager
Locate mid‑periphery midpoint with line tool and overlay label
Draw mid‑peripheral 300 × 800 μm rectangle
Add mid‑peripheral ROI to ROI manager
Repeat steps for all quadrants
Duplicate each ROI overlay to generate separate images
Save all ROI images

steps.title: Process ROI images
steps.instruction: Open each saved ROI image and duplicate it; convert to 8‑bit grayscale (Image → Type → 8‑bit); apply CLAHE (Process → Enhance Local Contrast) using a blocksize equal to the area to be equalized, histogram bins up to 256, and a maximum slope (default 1); denoise with Non‑local Means (Plugins → Non‑local means denoising) setting sigma as appropriate, smoothing factor = 1, using auto‑estimate or manual values; enhance edges with Unsharp Mask (Process → Filters → Unsharp Mask) setting radius (Gaussian blur SD) and mask weight = 1 (infinite), preview to optimise; remove salt‑and‑pepper noise with Median filter (Process → Filters → Median) choosing an appropriate radius and previewing; optionally subtract a constant background (Process → Math → Subtract) using the pixel value of the darkest background region; set threshold (Image → Adjust → Threshold) so the black‑white image matches the original appearance; convert to binary mask (Process → Binary → Convert to Mask) yielding foreground = 255 and background = 0; analyse particles (Analyze → Analyze Particles…) with size = 100‑Infinity μm² and Show = Masks; finally apply morphological filters (Plugins → MorphoLibJ → Morphological Filters) performing opening then closing with a square element of 1–2 pixels (or directional line elements) to smooth borders and fill holes.

substeps.instruction: Open saved ROI image and duplicate
Convert to 8‑bit grayscale
Apply CLAHE (blocksize = equalized area, histogram bins ≤ 256, max slope = 1)
Denoise with Non‑local Means (set sigma, smoothing factor = 1, auto‑estimate or manual)
Enhance edges with Unsharp Mask (set radius, mask weight = 1, preview)
Remove salt‑and‑pepper noise with Median filter (set radius, preview)
Subtract constant background (value = darkest background pixels)
Set threshold to obtain appropriate black‑white image
Convert to binary mask (foreground = 255, background = 0)
Analyze particles (size = 100‑Infinity μm², Show = Masks)
Apply morphological opening and closing (square element 1–2 px or directional line element)

steps.title: Calculate vessel density and lacunarity
steps.instruction: From the binary image, run Plugins → BoneJ → Fraction → Area/volume fraction to obtain vessel density (Db); run Plugins → MorphoLibJ → Analyze → Average Thickness for lacunarity; perform fractal analysis with Plugins → Fractal Analysis → FracLac – enable box‑counting (BC), lock white background, set max grid size to 30 px, check regression graphic, then click Scan; compute the average Db and lacunarity (L) across all ROIs.

steps.title: Skeletonize vessels
steps.instruction: With the binary image active, choose Plugins → Skeleton → Skeletonize (2D/3D) to reduce vessels to their centerline skeletons.

steps.title: Measure branch metrics
steps.instruction: On the skeleton image, run Plugins → BoneJ → Analyze Skeleton (no pruning, default options) to obtain average branch length, total number of branches, junctions, and triple points.

steps.title: Count cell clusters (CCs)
steps.instruction: Open each ROI image, select the Multi‑point tool, click each cell cluster (CC) to mark it, then measure the overlay to obtain the total CC count.

steps.title: Grade vascular disorganization
steps.instruction: Open the original retina image, outline disorganized vascular areas with the polygon selection tool, measure each outlined area as done for total vascularized area, and classify them as Grade 1 (significant noise but some ordered structure) or Grade 2 (almost completely disordered mesh) according to the provided examples.

steps.title: Compile summary of measurements
steps.instruction: Collect and record: retinal area (μm²), vascularized area fraction, percentage of Grade 1 and Grade 2 meshes, CC counts per ROI, vessel density (ratio), average branch length and diameter (μm), number of junctions and triple points, box‑counting fractal dimension (Db) and lacunarity (unitless); retain all generated images (whole retina, each ROI, binary masks, skeletons, FracLac outputs) for documentation.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been used and validated in the following research article: Feridooni et al. [72] Sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 2 inhibition ameliorates familial exudative vitreoretinopathy models. Journal of Biological Chemistry (Figures 2–5).
